facts.label: Há quanto tempo com for e since
facts.sub: Use for + período (for five years) e since + ponto de partida (since 2020) com have/has + particípio. Pergunte How long have you lived here?

facts.label: Por
facts.sub: Use for com uma quantidade de tempo: for two hours, for five years, for a long time. A frase fala de algo que começou no passado e continua: I have lived here for five years.

facts.label: Desde
facts.sub: Use since com um ponto de partida: since noon, since Monday, since 2020, since last year. É o momento em que começou: I have worked here since 2020.

compare.ask: I have lived here for five years.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “Moro aqui há cinco anos” com o presente.
compare.tip: Diga: “I have lived here for five years.”
compare.us: Em inglês, use have + particípio com for ou since: I have lived here for five years.

items.s: For is used with a period of time.
items.why: For two hours, for five years.

items.s: Since is used with a period of time.

answers: For is used with a period of time. → Verdadeiro (For two hours, for five years.)
Since is used with a period of time. → Falso (Since is used with a starting point.)
“I have lived here since 2020” is correct. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A rainy afternoon · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a gray, rainy afternoon in downtown Seattle. Water runs down the big windows of a small cafe. Freya sits at a table near the wall with her laptop. There are three empty cups next to her books. Her friend Ben comes in with a wet umbrella. He is surprised to see her there.

“Freya, you are here early! How long have you been here?” says Ben. “I have been here for two hours. I came at noon to finish my homework.” says Freya. “Wow! I have known this cafe since last year, but I never stay so long.” says Ben.

verbs.note: Know = conhecer, saber. Passado: knew. Quase não se usa no -ing: veja a forma ao lado.

items.why: Com she, o verbo leva -s: owns.
Com we, a forma base: stay.

solo: Aluno responde; você explica o porquê.

pages.title: Laboratório de sons · o som
pages.what: For soa “fôr” e fica fraco na frase. Since soa “sins”, com som de s no começo e no fim.
pages.how: Diga since como “sins”, sem vogal extra.
pages.tip: Compare for e since: for é curto, since é mais longo.

solo: Modele, peça repetição, depois uso livre.
